We’re looking at a Q4 push and want to increase our monthly hosted commit from 300M tokens to ~750M for the quarter (short-term bridge). Subject: Re: Q4 capacity bump & hosted commit question

Hi Elena —

Great timing — we can support a temporary uplift to ~750M tokens/month and propose the following quick path:

- Short amendment to your hosted plan that increases the monthly commit for Oct–Dec to 750M tokens.
- Two-tier pricing: the base commit retains the existing per-token rate; incremental tokens above your usual commit will be billed at a pre-agreed uplift (example: +22% for overage on the temporary bridge).
- Burst window: 10-minute burst buckets with soft throttling; we’ll guarantee an SLO for 99th percentile latency but enforce a per-minute QPS cap to protect multi-tenant infra.

I attached a first-pass amendment and a commit schedule with month-by-month expected consumption. If this looks OK I can route a DocuSign to procurement and loop Marissa for the commercial sign-off.

Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 capacity bump & hosted commit question — technical note

Hi all — quick technical addendum from SE side:

- For the uplift to behave predictably we recommend setting a per-route concurrency cap for your heaviest pipelines (recommendation: 80 concurrent streams for the critical endpoint) and enabling per-customer KV prefix caching.
- If you expect spiky bursts (eg: event-driven batch creation) increase the 10-minute burst window to 15 minutes for those flows; this can be enforced via a routing policy tied to a "burst" capacity pool.
- Rate limit defaults we suggest for the bridge: 18 rps sustained per second per shard, 2,200 tokens/sec token-generation ceiling per request. These numbers keep tail latency stable while you run at the increased commit.

I’m happy to run a short load test during the first week of Oct to validate.

—Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
[Attachment: SE-loadtest-checklist.txt]

Thanks Jordan & Ben — this is helpful. A few procurement/legal items before we can sign:

1) Can you provide a one-page summary that shows the delta in monthly spend and an example invoice for Oct under the amended rates?
2) We need explicit language around data retention and audit logs for the bridge period (we keep PII for 30 days, can you confirm logs are retained for 90 days and made available via the console/export?).
3) Is there a grace period if Marketly exceeds the 750M estimate mid-month? Procurment prefers a 72-hour buffer before aggressive throttling kicks in.

If those are OK we’ll route internally to legal and procurement.

Cheers,
Elena
